Misconfigurations.Title: Athena databases and workgroup configurations are created unencrypted at rest by default, they should be encrypted
Misconfigurations.Description: Data can be read if the Athena Database is compromised. Athena databases and workspace result sets should be encrypted at rests. These databases and query sets are generally derived from data in S3 buckets and should have the same level of at rest protection.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption at rest for Athena databases and workgroup configurations

Misconfigurations.Title: Athena workgroups should enforce configuration to prevent client disabling encryption
Misconfigurations.Description: Clients can ignore encryption requirements without enforced configuration. Athena workgroup configuration should be enforced to prevent client side changes to disable encryption settings.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce the configuration to prevent client overrides

Misconfigurations.Title: Config configuration aggregator should be using all regions for source
Misconfigurations.Description:
Sources that aren't covered by the aggregator are not include in the configuration. The configuration aggregator should be configured with all_regions for the source.
This will help limit the risk of any unmonitored configuration in regions that are thought to be unused.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set the aggregator to cover all regions

Misconfigurations.Title: DAX Cluster should always encrypt data at rest
Misconfigurations.Description: Data can be freely read if compromised. Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) encryption at rest provides an additional layer of data protection by helping secure your data from unauthorized access to the underlying storage.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption at rest for DAX Cluster

Misconfigurations.Title: Point in time recovery should be enabled to protect DynamoDB table
Misconfigurations.Description:
DynamoDB tables should be protected against accidentally or malicious write/delete actions by ensuring that there is adequate protection.
By enabling point-in-time-recovery you can restore to a known point in the event of loss of data.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable point in time recovery

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should prevent password reuse.
Misconfigurations.Description:
IAM account password policies should prevent the reuse of passwords.

The account password policy should be set to prevent using any of the last five used passwords.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Prevent password reuse in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one lowercase character.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including at least one lowercase character.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one number in the password.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including at least one number.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one symbol in the password.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including a symbol.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have requirement for at least one uppercase character.
Misconfigurations.Description:
,

IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords content including at least one uppercase character.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have expiry less than or equal to 90 days.
Misconfigurations.Description:
IAM account password policies should have a maximum age specified.

The account password policy should be set to expire passwords after 90 days or less.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit the password duration with an expiry in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Password policy should have minimum password length of 14 or more characters.
Misconfigurations.Description:
IAM account password policies should ensure that passwords have a minimum length.

The account password policy should be set to enforce minimum password length of at least 14 characters.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce longer, more complex passwords in the policy

Misconfigurations.Title: Lambda functions should have X-Ray tracing enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: X-Ray tracing enables end-to-end debugging and analysis of all function activity. This will allow for identifying bottlenecks, slow downs and timeouts.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable tracing

Misconfigurations.Title: Ensure that lambda function permission has a source arn specified
Misconfigurations.Description:
When the principal is an AWS service, the ARN of the specific resource within that service to grant permission to.
Without this, any resource from principal will be granted permission – even if that resource is from another account.
For S3, this should be the ARN of the S3 Bucket. For CloudWatch Events, this should be the ARN of the CloudWatch Events Rule. For API Gateway, this should be the ARN of the API
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Always provide a source arn for Lambda permissions

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should block public ACL
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should block public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By blocking, PUTs with fail if the object has any public ACL a.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable blocking any PUT calls with a public ACL specified

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should block public policy
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 bucket policy should have block public policy to prevent users from putting a policy that enable public access.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Prevent policies that allow public access being PUT

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Data should be versioned
Misconfigurations.Description:
Versioning in Amazon S3 is a means of keeping multiple variants of an object in the same bucket.

You can use the S3 Versioning feature to preserve, retrieve, and restore every version of every object stored in your buckets.

With versioning you can recover more easily from both unintended user actions and application failures.

When you enable versioning, also keep in mind the potential costs of storing noncurrent versions of objects. To help manage those costs, consider setting up an S3 Lifecycle configuration.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable versioning to protect against accidental/malicious removal or modification

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access Block should Ignore Public ACL
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should ignore public ACLs on buckets and any objects they contain. By ignoring rather than blocking, PUT calls with public ACLs will still be applied but the ACL will be ignored.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable ignoring the application of public ACLs in PUT calls

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Buckets not publicly accessible through ACL.
Misconfigurations.Description: Buckets should not have ACLs that allow public access
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Don't use canned ACLs or switch to private acl

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Access block should restrict public bucket to limit access
Misconfigurations.Description: S3 buckets should restrict public policies for the bucket. By enabling, the restrict_public_buckets, only the bucket owner and AWS Services can access if it has a public policy.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit the access to public buckets to only the owner or AWS Services (eg; CloudFront)

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 buckets should each define an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block
Misconfigurations.Description: The "block public access" settings in S3 override individual policies that apply to a given bucket, meaning that all public access can be controlled in one central types for that bucket. It is therefore good practice to define these settings for each bucket in order to clearly define the public access that can be allowed for it.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Define a aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block for the given bucket to control public access policies

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM groups should have MFA enforcement activated.
Misconfigurations.Description: IAM groups should be protected with multi factor authentication to add safe guards to password compromise.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use terraform-module/enforce-mfa/aws to ensure that MFA is enforced

Misconfigurations.Title: The "root" account has unrestricted access to all resources in the AWS account. It is highly recommended that the use of this account be avoided.
Misconfigurations.Description: The root user has unrestricted access to all services and resources in an AWS account. We highly recommend that you avoid using the root user for daily tasks. Minimizing the use of the root user and adopting the principle of least privilege for access management reduce the risk of accidental changes and unintended disclosure of highly privileged credentials.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use lower privileged accounts instead, so only required privileges are available.

Misconfigurations.Title: The root user has complete access to all services and resources in an AWS account. AWS Access Keys provide programmatic access to a given account.
Misconfigurations.Description: CIS recommends that all access keys be associated with the root user be removed. Removing access keys associated with the root user limits vectors that the account can be compromised by. Removing the root user access keys also encourages the creation and use of role-based accounts that are least privileged.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use lower privileged accounts instead, so only required privileges are available.

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM policies should not be granted directly to users.
Misconfigurations.Description: CIS recommends that you apply IAM policies directly to groups and roles but not users. Assigning privileges at the group or role level reduces the complexity of access management as the number of users grow. Reducing access management complexity might in turn reduce opportunity for a principal to inadvertently receive or retain excessive privileges.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Grant policies at the group level instead.

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 DNS Compliant Bucket Names
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures that S3 buckets have DNS complaint bucket names.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Recreate S3 bucket to use - instead of . in S3 bucket names

Misconfigurations.Title: IAM Pass Role Filtering
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures any IAM pass role attached to roles are flagged and warned.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Resolve permission escalations by denying pass role'

Misconfigurations.Title: Disallow unrestricted S3 IAM Policies
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensure that the creation of the unrestricted S3 IAM policies is disallowed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Create more restrictive S3 policies

Misconfigurations.Title: Reduce unnecessary unauthorized access or information disclosure of S3 buckets.
Misconfigurations.Description: Unnecessary access to S3 buckets can lead to unauthorized access or information disclosure.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Allowing Get* along with Put* on all Resources can potentially allow unauthorized access and/or information disclosure from sensitive buckets.

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage containers in blob storage mode should not have public access
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage container public access should be off. It can be configured for blobs only, containers and blobs or off entirely. The default is off, with no public access.
Explicitly overriding publicAccess to anything other than off should be avoided.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable public access to storage containers

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage accounts should be configured to only accept transfers that are over secure connections
Misconfigurations.Description:
You can configure your storage account to accept requests from secure connections only by setting the Secure transfer required property for the storage account.
When you require secure transfer, any requests originating from an insecure connection are rejected.
Microsoft recommends that you always require secure transfer for all of your storage accounts.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Only allow secure connection for transferring data into storage accounts

Misconfigurations.Title: When using Queue Services for a storage account, logging should be enabled.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage Analytics logs detailed information about successful and failed requests to a storage service.
This information can be used to monitor individual requests and to diagnose issues with a storage service.
Requests are logged on a best-effort basis.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for Queue Services

Misconfigurations.Title: Trusted Microsoft Services should have bypass access to Storage accounts
Misconfigurations.Description:
Some Microsoft services that interact with storage accounts operate from networks that can't be granted access through network rules.
To help this type of service work as intended, allow the set of trusted Microsoft services to bypass the network rules
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Allow Trusted Microsoft Services to bypass

Misconfigurations.Title: The minimum TLS version for Storage Accounts should be TLS1_2 or higher
Misconfigurations.Description:
Azure Storage supports four versions of the TLS protocol: 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3.
Azure Storage uses TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 on public HTTPS endpoints, while TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are still supported for backward compatibility.
This check will warn if the minimum TLS version is set lower than TLS1_2. TLS1_2 and TLS1_3 are both allowed.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use a more recent TLS version for the storage account

Misconfigurations.Title: The default action on Storage account network rules should be set to deny
Misconfigurations.Description:
The default_action for network rules should come into effect when no other rules are matched.
The default action should be set to Deny.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set network rules to deny

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have blob soft delete enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Blob soft delete protects blob data from being accidentally or erroneously modified or deleted.
When blob soft delete is enabled, deleted blobs are retained in the system for a specified retention period.
During the retention period, you can restore a soft-deleted blob to its state at the time it was deleted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable soft delete for blobs with an appropriate retention period

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have logging enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage Analytics logs detailed information about successful and failed requests to a storage service.
This information can be used to monitor individual requests and to diagnose issues with a storage service.
Logging should be enabled for at least one storage service type.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for at least one storage service (Queue, Table, or Blob)

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should use geo-redundant replication
Misconfigurations.Description:
Geo-redundant storage (GRS) replicates your data to a secondary region that is hundreds of miles away from the primary region.
This provides an additional level of durability for your data in the event of a complete regional outage or a disaster.
Options include GRS, RAGRS, GZRS, and RAGZRS for geo-redundancy.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Configure storage account to use geo-redundant replication (GRS, RAGRS, GZRS, or RAGZRS)

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have secure transfer and minimum TLS version configured
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage accounts should enforce HTTPS for secure data transfer and use a minimum TLS version of 1.2.
This ensures that logs and data stored in the storage account are encrypted in transit.
Azure Storage encrypts all data at rest by default, but transport encryption is also critical.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable secure transfer and set minimum TLS version to TLS1_2

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should use customer-managed keys for encryption
Misconfigurations.Description:
Storage accounts should use customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption to provide additional control over the encryption keys.
Customer-managed keys allow you to create, rotate, disable, and revoke access controls.
They also provide greater flexibility to audit the encryption keys that are used to protect your data.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Configure customer-managed keys for storage account encryption

Misconfigurations.Title: Storage account should have infrastructure encryption enabled
Misconfigurations.Description:
Infrastructure encryption provides an additional layer of encryption at the infrastructure level.
When infrastructure encryption is enabled, data in the storage account is encrypted twice -
once at the service level and once at the infrastructure level with two different encryption algorithms.
This provides double encryption for enhanced security.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable infrastructure encryption for storage account

Misconfigurations.Title: A firewall rule should not allow unrestricted ingress from any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Description: Opening up ports to allow connections from the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set a more restrictive cidr range

Misconfigurations.Title: VPC flow logs should be enabled for all subnetworks
Misconfigurations.Description: VPC flow logs record information about all traffic, which is a vital tool in reviewing anomalous traffic.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable VPC flow logs

Misconfigurations.Title: Disable project-wide SSH keys for all instances
Misconfigurations.Description: Use of project-wide SSH keys means that a compromise of any one of these key pairs can result in all instances being compromised. It is recommended to use instance-level keys.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable project-wide SSH keys

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not have public IP addresses
Misconfigurations.Description: Instances should not be publicly exposed to the internet
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Remove public IP

Misconfigurations.Title: Disable serial port connectivity for all instances
Misconfigurations.Description: When serial port access is enabled, the access is not governed by network security rules meaning the port can be exposed publicly.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable serial port access

Misconfigurations.Title: VM disks should be encrypted with Customer Supplied Encryption Keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Using unmanaged keys makes rotation and general management difficult.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use managed keys

Misconfigurations.Title: Disks should be encrypted with customer managed encryption keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Using unmanaged keys makes rotation and general management difficult.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use managed keys to encrypt disks.

Misconfigurations.Title: A firewall rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set a more restrictive cidr range

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not override the project setting for OS Login
Misconfigurations.Description: OS Login automatically revokes the relevant SSH keys when an IAM user has their access revoked.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable OS Login at project level and remove instance-level overrides

Misconfigurations.Title: The encryption key used to encrypt a compute disk has been specified in plaintext.
Misconfigurations.Description: Sensitive values such as raw encryption keys should not be included in your Terraform code, and should be stored securely by a secrets manager.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Reference a managed key rather than include the key in raw format.

Misconfigurations.Title: SSL policies should enforce secure versions of TLS
Misconfigurations.Description: TLS versions prior to 1.2 are outdated and insecure. You should use 1.2 as aminimum version.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enforce a minimum TLS version of 1.2

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should have Shielded VM VTPM enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: The virtual TPM provides numerous security measures to your VM.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Shielded VM VTPM

Misconfigurations.Title: OS Login should be enabled at project level
Misconfigurations.Description: OS Login automatically revokes the relevant SSH keys when an IAM user has their access revoked.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable OS Login at project level

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not have IP forwarding enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Disabling IP forwarding ensures the instance can only receive packets addressed to the instance and can only send packets with a source address of the instance.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Disable IP forwarding

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should not use the default service account
Misconfigurations.Description: The default service account has full project access. Instances should instead be assigned the minimal access they need.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Remove use of default service account

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should have Shielded VM integrity monitoring enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Integrity monitoring helps you understand and make decisions about the state of your VM instances.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Shielded VM Integrity Monitoring

Misconfigurations.Title: Instances should have Shielded VM secure boot enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Secure boot helps ensure that the system only runs authentic software.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Shielded VM secure boot

Misconfigurations.Title: RDP Access Is Not Restricted
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules should restrict RDP (TCP/3389) access to specific IP ranges. Open RDP access can be a security risk.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Restrict RDP (TCP port 3389) ingress in firewall rules. Only allow trusted IP ranges or use Identity-Aware Proxy for RDP access.

Misconfigurations.Title: SSH Access Is Not Restricted
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules should restrict SSH (TCP/22) access to specific IPs. Open SSH can be a security risk.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Restrict SSH (TCP port 22) access in firewall rules to known IP addresses or ranges. Avoid open 0.0.0.0/0 access for SSH.

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Network Using Firewall Rule that Allows All Ports
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules should not be wide open to all ports. Lock down rules to only required ports.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Modify firewall rules that allow all ports to restrict to only required ports. Use separate rules for specific port ranges as needed, instead of a single overly broad rule.

Misconfigurations.Title: Disable Default Firewall Rules
Misconfigurations.Description:
Ensures that Google Cloud's default firewall rules are disabled, as they may be overly permissive and pose security risks.
The default network comes with pre-populated firewall rules that allow broad access and should be replaced with more restrictive custom rules.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Replace default firewall rules with custom, more restrictive rules appropriate for your security requirements

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Network Using Firewall Rule that Allows Large Port Range
Misconfigurations.Description: Firewall rules allowing broad port ranges can be risky. Ensure rules are as specific as possible.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Limit firewall rules to necessary port ranges only. If a wide range is specified, consider splitting into smaller ranges or specific ports needed for your application.

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Subnetwork with Private Google Access Disabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Private Google Access allows instances in a subnet to reach Google APIs and services via internal IP, which should be enabled for private networks.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable Private Google Access on subnets. In Terraform, set `private_ip_google_access = true` in the `google_compute_subnetwork` resource.

Misconfigurations.Title: Google Compute Subnetwork Logging Disabled
Misconfigurations.Description: Flow logs for subnets should be enabled to capture network traffic details for security analysis.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable VPC Flow Logs for subnets. In Terraform, set `enable_flow_logs = true` in the `google_compute_subnetwork` resource.

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudWatch log groups should be encrypted using CMK
Misconfigurations.Description: CloudWatch log groups are encrypted by default, however, to get the full benefit of controlling key rotation and other KMS aspects a KMS CMK should be used.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable CMK encryption of CloudWatch Log Groups

Misconfigurations.Title: DynamoDB tables should use at rest encryption with a Customer Managed Key
Misconfigurations.Description: Using AWS managed keys does not allow for fine grained control. DynamoDB tables are encrypted by default using AWS managed encryption keys. To increase control of the encryption and control the management of factors like key rotation, use a Customer Managed Key.
Misconfigurations.Message: Table encryption explicitly uses the default KMS key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable server side encryption with a customer managed key

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Bucket Logging
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures S3 bucket logging is enabled for S3 buckets
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add a logging block to the resource to enable access logging

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
Misconfigurations.Description:
Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your S3 buckets. To gain greater control over encryption, such as key rotation, access policies, and auditability, use customer managed keys (CMKs) with SSE-KMS.
Note that SSE-KMS is not supported for S3 server access logging destination buckets; in such cases, use SSE-S3 instead.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK)
